how_customers_find_and_choose: Members, donors and families come through personal contact, trust in the people running the institution and word of mouth
Donors want to see exactly what was done with their contribution, with photos and short reports
Communities share announcements and appeals through chat groups and community leaders
Public sector buyers choose suppliers through formal tenders and documented past work
what_works_now: A short, honest report of what was done with funds or effort, with photos and no exaggeration
A clear message for each appeal: who, what, how much is needed and how it will be used
A saved list of members or donors for updates, with their consent
Written records of contributions, expenses and decisions shared with those who gave
For funeral and community services: a calm, respectful and quick response with clear arrangements
For contractors: a file of past work, certificates and references ready for tenders
Regular updates to members or families after an event or service
outdated_or_weak: Pressure or emotional manipulation in appeals
Unclear accounts of where donations went
Using photos of vulnerable people without their permission
Printed posters as the main way to reach people
Treating a tender as a cold sales pitch rather than a documented bid

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Charity and community giving peaks in Ramadan and around Eid; zakat and sadaqah shape donation timing
Charities and trusts are registered with the relevant authority; the owner confirms specifics
Government supply follows tender rules and payment cycles that can be slow
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Charity and community activity needs permission from the relevant authority; the owner confirms specifics
Community groups are often built around nationality, faith or neighbourhood
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Charities follow registration and reporting rules by province; the owner confirms specifics
Volunteers are central; donors expect online giving and clear reports

never_assume: Permission to share photos of the people helped
